key_points: The initial request (CL-01, stakeholder SH-CS) framed the issue as a communication gap needing AI-drafted apology replies; this framing was contradicted by E-01 through E-05.

Root cause was established as a technical misconfiguration: SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and never rolled it back (E-01), confirmed by a before/after PSP log pattern (E-02), a matching jump in ledger duplicate captures (E-03), a matching spike in support tickets (E-04), and SH-PAY's own account (E-05).
Hypothesis H-GATEWAY-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED was supported by the evidence; H-COMMUNICATION-GAP, H-CLIENT-DOUBLE-SUBMIT, H-FALSE-POSITIVE-PERCEPTION and H-PSP-SIDE-RETRY-BUG were all rejected.
A query of the charge ledger (E-08) found 4 duplicate-capture orders still open and unrefunded: O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing explicitly held back; this followed a DEFINE gate result of CONDITIONAL_PASS, which deferred unresolved items as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than blocking release.

The protected fix action itself (set_capture_idempotency on the gateway) is not part of what was released; it still requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation (constraint K-GW, E-07) and resolution of VOB-U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF before it can be executed.

Idempotency-key enforcement remains disabled at the time of this release (per E-01 and assumption A-ENFORCEMENT-STILL-OFF), so new duplicate charges may continue to occur until the fix is actually applied.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than a full pass; some open questions were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) instead of being resolved before release.
VOB-U-LATENCY-TRADEOFF (whether re-enabling the key would bring back the original latency problem) is still open, but it only blocks the actual gateway change, which is outside this release's scope.

VOB-R-2 (how many duplicate-capture orders still need a refund, and whether any were already refunded) touches the released analysis scope but is marked non-critical, partly because the completeness of the charge-ledger data (DA-CHG) is marked UNKNOWN.
Once applied, the gateway config fix will stop new duplicates going forward, but it will not by itself remediate orders that were already double-captured since 2026-09-09.
Completeness of the gateway config-audit log (DA-CFG) and the charge ledger (DA-CHG) is marked UNKNOWN, so some duplicate orders or config-change records could be missing from the analysis.
The unknown U-AFFECTED-ORDERS-REMEDIATION is open, meaning already-issued refunds cannot be reliably distinguished from orders that still need one.
Whether the H-CAPTURE handoff (shop to PSP) is actually delivered and semantically valid is UNKNOWN, per a finding from the CONDITIONAL_PASS gate.
output.summary: The requester (SH-CS) originally asked for an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers charged twice, framing the problem as a communication gap (CL-01). Investigation across the gateway config-audit log, PSP capture log, charge ledger and support tickets instead established the real root cause: payments engineer SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway on 2026-09-09 for temporary latency debugging and never rolled it back (E-01), which let routine gateway-timeout capture retries post as real second charges — shown by a before/after PSP pattern (E-02), a matching jump in ledger duplicate-captures (E-03), a matching spike in support tickets (E-04), and corroborated directly by SH-PAY (E-05). The communication-gap hypothesis was rejected; the gateway-misconfiguration hypothesis was supported. The released scope covers the read-only analysis work (reviewing DA-CHG, DA-TKT, DA-CFG, DA-PSP) that established and quantified this problem, plus identification of 4 still-open unrefunded duplicate orders (E-08). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, following a CONDITIONAL_PASS DEFINE-gate result: the actual fix (re-enabling the gateway's idempotency key, a protected action requiring SH-OPS runtime confirmation) is not part of this release because a high-impact open question (will re-enabling it reintroduce the original latency problem?) must be resolved first, and that question's blocking scope sits outside what was released. Several other open questions were documented as known limitations rather than resolved, so this release ships the diagnosis and partial remediation groundwork, not the completed fix.
